finding_key: packages/backend/src/datasource/datasource.service.ts::datasource tls connections disable certificate verification (`rejectunauthorized: false`), so a network attacker can mitm and capture the decrypted datasource credentials
evidence: The code as supplied does contain `ssl: ds.sslEnabled ? { rejectUnauthorized: false } : false` in `DataSourceService.createClient` (packages/backend/src/datasource/datasource.service.ts, in the `createClient` literal immediately above the newly added `types: { getTypeParser: datasourceTypeParser }` line), and `decrypt(ds.password)` is sent over that connection. `CreateDataSourceDto`/`UpdateDataSourceDto` (datasource.dto.ts) expose only `sslEnabled` — no CA, servername, or reject flag — so there is indeed no way for a caller to obtain a verified TLS session, exactly as the claim states. The defect is pre-existing rather than introduced by this diff (the diff only appends the `types` option to the same object literal), but the claim is accurate about the code as written and does not misdescribe the mechanism.
